name: How do I choose between a full remodel and a layout-only change?

mainEntity.name: How do I choose between a full kitchen remodel and a layout-only change?
mainEntity.text: How do I choose between a full kitchen remodel and a layout-only change?

acceptedAnswer.text: The choice depends on what is actually causing the problem. If the kitchen looks dated but works well, a cosmetic update may be enough. If the room functions poorly because the layout is awkward, then a layout change is more appropriate. If the cabinets are damaged, the plumbing and electrical are outdated, or the appliances no longer fit the space well, a full remodel may make more sense because the project is already disruptive. Layout-only changes can be a smart middle ground when the structure is sound and the main issue is flow. A full remodel is usually better when the current kitchen has multiple problems at once, such as poor circulation, bad storage, and worn-out finishes. The best decision comes from separating appearance issues from functional issues. If the space frustrates daily use, it is worth investing in the layout rather than just covering up the problem.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose a layout-only change if the room functions poorly but the cabinets, finishes, and systems are still workable. Choose a full remodel if the kitchen has outdated infrastructure, failing materials, or a layout problem that cannot be solved without replacing most of the room.
